overview: Learning Blocks: learning games for young children in a quiet classroom of their own: Reading, Numbers and Logic, spoken aloud, with prizes to take home.
Press the Learning Blocks button (or /learn) to go in, and walk through the portal to come home with everything you went in with.

0.2.2: The classroom can't be entered from a PvP Dimensions arena: going in from there mixed the arena's kit up with your own things. A daily schedule waits, and sends you in as soon as you leave the arena.
0.2.1: Number tiles are answered as letters are: break one loose, carry it, and place it in the gap on the board. A wrong one flies back to its spot to be tried again. Bob's number cards are still clicked.
"Nice reading!" is said only after reading; Numbers and Logic rounds get the other cheers.
The prize chest by the portal is always there, and sparkles while a prize is waiting. Opened before anything is earned, it says Nothing yet.
Learning Blocks is on the first page of the action menu, and its buttons show the classroom's own toys.
The letter a has a new recording.
0.2.0: Phonics is now Learning Blocks, and Reading is one of three subjects. 0.2.0 starts fresh: progress, toys and schedules from Phonics do not carry over, and /phonics is gone; use /learn.
Subjects: Reading, Numbers and Logic take turns, with a hello and a coloured board edge for each. /learn subjects turns a child's subjects on and off, and a daily schedule can ask for some of each.

Numbers, stages N0 to N2: which block says it, quick looks, counting creatures out of the button, make a number, beds for kittens, counting your Toybox, scenes, Bob with number cards, pens, towers, number lines, and the picture with that many.
Wooden number tiles, 0 to 20, with dots on the sides; and symbol tiles, plus, minus and equals.

Logic, stages L0 to L3: sorting animals into pens, same or different, patterns (what comes next, find the mistake, copy it, notes), odd one out, what's missing, putting things in order, and Bob with word cards.
Reading, stages 9 to 14: magic e, vowel teams, ng and nk, r-controlled vowels, ow, ay, igh and oi, and big words in chunks (cat|fish).
Mastery: a word, number or pattern counts as learned after clean days, not one good try. Stages come in bands (1a, 1b), and old words come back for review.
Tricky words, big and little letters, plurals and two-word phrases, and Read it rounds.
Tell Bob: build a sentence from word cards and Bob acts it out; silly sentences from the action menu.
Plushies and toys to earn, kept in the Toybox tab, and props and picture cards around the room.
Sky, weather and feelings: some words change your own sky, and creatures show how they feel.
Learning together: two or three children in one classroom, taking turns, with team-up rounds. /learn join asks; the other says yes or no.
The portal: walk through it to go home. While lessons are left it stays dark with the count over it.
For grown-ups: daily schedules by weekday, /learn progress with an export, /learn home, /learn give for a lost plushie or toy, /learn plots prune, and the sampler (/learn try) for any kind of round.
A child who gets stuck is sent home safely, and the log says why.
0.1.0: A classroom with one puzzle: _ A T, three letters to try, and a button that reads the word out.
CAT brings a cat, BAT a bat, HAT a hat on your head.
Every letter, word and cheer is spoken, with big captions that light up each word as it is said.
Letter tiles say their sound when placed, picked up or hit.
Prizes to take home for new words, streaks and more, set by the server in the prizes file.
A book, My Words, that lists every word you have read.
Operators can change every prize in game with /learn prizes, items and all.
Captions can be turned off, made smaller, or moved; they now sit at the top by default.
A prize held back by the daily cap is paid on a later day instead of lost.
Forty more words in five stages, one short vowel at a time: pigs, puppies, beds, fireworks and more.
You move up a stage once you have read every word in yours.
Tiles are broken and placed like any block: knock one loose, pick it up, place it in the gap.
Vowel tiles say their short sound; a picture of the word hangs over the board.
What a word does now comes out of the button: creatures hop out, items fly to you.
A wrong tile flies back to its place; placing into a full gap swaps; the floor never gets muddled.
The prize chest shows what is waiting. Moving up a stage starts fresh.
Grown-ups can send a child for a number of lessons, and click the picture to hear the word again.
Wrong words do something sillier: a hat bonks you, the fox runs off, TEN throws snowballs at you.
Letter sounds and My words: hear every letter, the vowels, and the words you have read, from anywhere.
Long captions wrap onto a second line instead of running off the screen.
When a word is sounded out, its vowel is the one from that word's own recording.
Situations: now and then the room acts out a little problem, and one of your words fixes it.
Fixed: a child with prizes waiting could sometimes never leave the classroom.
Letters first: new readers start by matching sounds to letters, with a chant for each one.
Prizes fly into the chest where you can see them, and the haul grows on top.
The room says its most common lines in several different ways.
The My Words book is gone; the My words screen does its job.
New words: zap, yap, nap, ram, ham, jam, wag, rag, van, sit, win, zip, sip, hop, pop, mop, rod, cod, yum, hum, gum, bug, tug, cut, hut, sun, leg, beg, gem, fed, vet, web.
New kinds of round: change the last sound (map, mat, man) or the vowel in the middle (cat, cot, cut).
Letter names: each letter on the Letter sounds screen has a Name button.
Thirteen new situations, from bouncing puppies to a stuck villager.
Two-letter tiles (sh, ch, th, ck, qu, ll, ss, ff, zz) and a Two-letter sounds screen.
Build-it rounds: the whole word from its own tiles.
Stages 6 to 8: double letters, sh ch th qu, and blends, with 49 new words.
